description: A Tibetan settlement in the Biligiri Rangan hills — out over the Dhimbam hairpins, back down the Kadambur ghat.
story: Biker's Club CBE's one-day September ride, and the destination is one that most people who have ridden the Dhimbam road have never heard of. Dhondenling is a Tibetan refugee settlement at Odeyarpalya near Kollegal — established in 1974, around 4,500 people living across 22 village clusters on 3,121 acres of the Biligiri Rangan hills, 3,345 ft up. Eight monasteries sit inside it; the largest is Dzogchen, rebuilt here from 1984 after the original in Tibet was destroyed by fire, and home to over 200 monks today. The route earns the early start. Out through Sathyamangalam, up the Dhimbam hairpins into the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, over the Karnataka border and on to Kollegal, then the climb to the settlement. The way back takes a different line down — Germalam, then the Kadambur ghat, which drops out of the hills on the Sathyamangalam side and runs home from there. Assemble 5:30 AM at Coimbatore, wheels rolling at 6:00. Faith, roads, people, mountains — the poster's own list, and a fair summary of the day.
_compliments: Off the poster's inclusions list, in its order, with ONE deliberate omission: the poster's "All brand bikes welcome" is an eligibility rule, not something you receive, so it does not belong in a list of what the ride comes with.
